page.layout: One column of verse, set in italic, with lines indented in groups of four; no marginal notes. Running head at top centre-right, page number at top left, catchword at lower right.

p.i: Non ille comta molle nitens coma Te, nec Sabæis ambit odoribus. Non improbus captat dolosis Illecebris animum rebellem.
Sed luce ferri lucifica minax, Pectúsq; squamis asper aheneis, Aut spumeos frenos fatigans Quadrupedis præeuntis Euros.
Qualis virentem Mars prope Strymona Exercet acrem quadrijugúm fugam, Seu Parthia cladem feroci Seu gelido meditatur Istro.
Nec tu labores despicis anxios, Tenaëa dignam scilicet indolem, Nec credulum pascens amorem Spe sterili crucias animum, amicum,
Seu per procellis fœta nivalibus Prærupta & alpes agmen agit feras: Seu per tumentes imbre fluctus, Seu validas labefactat arces.
Tu dux per Alpes pandis iter feras. Amnes frementes pontibus alligas. Tu claustra portarum revellis, Et peragis sine cæde regna.
Quocunque iustas te duce verterit Cossæus iras, pallidas anteit Pallor, tremor, terror, pauorque, Depositis male fortis armis.

page.notes: The stanza break after every four lines is taken from the printed indentation. "Coffæus" is read as "Cossæus" (the ff is a double s). "Tu" at lower right is the catchword for the next page. "amicum," in the line "Spe sterili crucias animum, amicum," is set in smaller type inside the text, so it is not a marginal note. "Sabæis" and the other Latin words are copied as printed. Some letters in the scan are faint, especially in "Aut spumeos" and "Alpes", which carry an ornamental flourish; these were read from the printed letters and not checked against another copy.
